subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Slider-Crank: The Engine's Heart
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Slider-Crank: The Engine's Heart.

hook.text: Every piston engine turns a slider-crank billions of times in its life.

buildup.text: A crank rotates. A connecting rod links it to a piston that slides.

discovery.text: Combustion pushes the piston down. The crank converts that push to rotation.

twist.text: The piston doesn't move at constant speed — it surges and slows each stroke.

climax.text: Every car, lawnmower, and diesel generator relies on this mechanism.

punchline.text: Slide to spin — the oldest engine trick still runs the world.

quiz.question: Why doesn't a piston move at constant speed during each stroke?
options: Combustion pressure varies throughout the stroke
The crank geometry creates non-uniform velocity from its circular path
Friction between the piston and cylinder varies with position
